faq.a: Zed is a code editor built entirely in Rust for low-latency, native performance, as opposed to the Electron shell used by editors like VS Code and Cursor. Its 1.0 release introduced Parallel Agents, letting multiple AI agents work on different parts of a codebase at the same time.
faq.q: What is Zed?

faq.a: Zed has a free Personal plan, but it caps Zed-hosted AI use at 2,000 accepted edit predictions unless you bring your own API keys. Paid tiers are Pro at $10 per month and Business at $30 per seat per month for teams that need governance controls.

faq.a: Both support running agents in parallel: Zed's Parallel Agents lets agents work on separate parts of a codebase simultaneously, while Cursor also offers parallel agents plus cloud agents for offloading longer tasks. If you specifically want external agents like Claude Agent or Codex running inside the editor itself, Zed's Agent Client Protocol gives it an edge.

choose_a: ✅ You want a faster, lighter editor since Zed is built entirely in Rust instead of being an Electron or VS Code fork.
✅ You want to run multiple AI agents at once on different parts of your codebase using Zed's Parallel Agents feature.
✅ You want to plug external agents like Claude Agent, Codex, OpenCode, or Cursor directly into your editor via Zed's Agent Client Protocol.
✅ You manage a team and want simple, published per-seat pricing for AI governance instead of a shared usage pool tied to another product.
choose_b: ✅ You want to stay in a VS Code-based environment so your existing extensions, keybindings, and workflows carry over.
✅ You want automated PR review and bug-catching built in through Bugbot alongside agentic coding.
✅ You want cloud agents and cloud dev environments you can trigger with /in-cloud to offload long-running tasks.
✅ You want a bundled Grok model plus the flexibility to add third-party models via MCP servers and custom rules.
